review.reason: Candidate 40 is the strongest balanced choice. The numbered preview shows a compact, irregular property with folded routing: G1 sits near T2 and G2 near T3, with varied hole orientations and playable grass between selective groves. Hole 1 is a 483-yard reachable par 5 with substantial water alongside the route; a staged line away from the shoreline is credible, while chasing a chance to reach in two carries more risk. Hole 2 is a 397-yard dogleg-left par 4 with a meaningful choice between following the bend and taking a more aggressive line near its substantial lake. The one-shot simulated reach is evidence of an opportunity, not proof that the shortcut is reliably safe. Hole 3 is a dry 227-yard par 3, offering a long distance-control test without another forced water carry. The par-5/4/3 sequence and mix of two shoreline decisions with a dry long par 3 provide excellent within-round variety. Reachable water-side par 5s recur in recent rounds, including course 110, so novelty is good rather than exceptional; the added wet dogleg and dry par 3 make this combination meaningfully different. Simulated shots-to-green of 2/1/1 and 43/43/55 safe tee options support a challenging but playable round, while the preview shows usable landing routes. No clearly warranted geometry change is needed.
